messages:
Alex: FYI i'm seeing a token id shift when converting a SentencePiece model to BPE. Runs fine locally but evals show a perplexity jump on the convo & code suites.
Maria: which conversion tool did you use? the internal hf-to-redwood script or tokenizers CLI?
Alex: used our hf-to-redwood converter (tools/convert_hf_tokenizer.py) with the default fallback for merges. The symptom looks like reserved/special tokens getting appended to the vocab end, shifting ids. Repro steps attached.
Alex: ```bash
python tools/convert_hf_tokenizer.py --src /mnt/models/spm_xl --dst /tmp/bpe_xl --emit-map map.json
cat /tmp/bpe_xl/map.json | jq .special_tokens
```
Kai: hmm, that smells like config.json's "vocab_size" vs actual tokenizer merges mismatch. SentencePiece keeps reserved tokens in a different logical order than BPE, so naive remap can shift everything. Did you inspect tokenizer.json order?
Priya: Also watch unicode normalization — SPM pieces can include invisible joiners (ZWJ) or NBSP which end up as separate pieces and change merge ordering. Any concrete token examples?
Alex: Example: original spm pieces include "▁`" and "▁`\u200d" — after conversion we ended up with those forms split and the ids swapped (backshift by +3). On the codeeval suite that produced many off-by-one token mismatches, lowering exact-match.
convert-bot: automated upload: map.json saved to /artifacts/1945678901/map.json
Maria: If our conversion emits special tokens at the end of the new vocab, everything after them will shift. We should preserve SPM piece ordering and explicitly assign original ids for specials during remap.
Kai: quick diagnostic: run encode on same sample text pre/post conversion and diff. Example script: 
```py
from tokenizers import Tokenizer
s = 'def foo(): return 1\\n'
old = Tokenizer.from_file('spm_tokenizer.json')
new = Tokenizer.from_file('bpe_tokenizer.json')
print('old', old.encode(s).ids)
print('new', new.encode(s).ids)
```
Priya: Important: the KV cache and embedding lookup for quantized runtime assumes stable id->embedding mapping. Even a small id shift causes wrong embeddings to be used and looks like quality regression in generation.
Alex: I tried manually remapping special token ids to match the original mapping and reran the micro-eval; perplexity improved but emoji + skin-tone sequences still tokenized differently.
Maria: Could be HF export chose NFC while SPM uses NFKC normalization; difference shows up for composed glyphs. Try forcing nfkc in the normalizer stage during conversion and re-run token diffs.
Priya: For rollout gating, propose adding a canary eval that runs our chat-template prompts, a code exact-match suite, and fails the conversion if top-1 exact-match drops > 2% or perplexity increases beyond threshold.
Kai: Agreed. I'll add an eval-bot job that runs on every conversion PR. @Priya can you add a small unit test that diffs token ids for a set of anchor sentences to catch reorderings? :thumbsup:
Priya: will add tests + a small fixture with SPM edgecases (ZWJ, NBSP, emoji modifiers, backticks) and assert identical id sequences after conversion.
Alex: Thanks — I'll hold off the big quantized benchmark run until we confirm mapping/test pass. Happy to pair after stand to root the unicode differences.
eval-bot: spawned job 1945678901-quant-eval; status queued
Maria: filing a short reproduction note in #eng-ml with steps and map.json link.
